_meta.description: Hand-maintained expected-yield baseline for scripts/check_yield.py. min_expected is a conservative floor -- comfortably below the lowest legitimate weekly count seen for that source -- not a target, so it doesn't false-positive on a genuinely quiet week. A source at status 'ok' with events below its floor gets flagged. Sources with min_expected: 0 are known to have genuinely empty weeks (confirmed against v1's dual-write run, which predates v2's under-collection) and are excluded from the yield-floor check entirely -- only the provenance and manifest/file-agreement checks apply to them.
_meta.baseline_source: git show 728633b:data/2026-07-20/_manifest.json (v1 Mac dual-write, the last known-complete collection of a real week before v2's Collection Routine began silently zeroing sources under budget pressure -- see docs/COLLECTION_YIELD_INVESTIGATION.md)
_meta.revisit: Each quarterly source-revalidation pass (see philadelphia-sources/SKILL.md Maintenance section) and whenever a source gains a deterministic parser -- raise min_expected once real yield is confirmed stable under the new method.

cinespeak.note: A deterministic parser now backs this source (scripts/event_parsers/cinespeak.py, plain Gutenberg block markup on /cinema/) -- confirmed live 2026-07-29: 1 event for the real week of 2026-08-03. Historical range is thin and genuinely variable (1-2/week in v1 and v2 run A, 0 confirmed for this specific week) -- kept at 0 rather than 1 to avoid false-positiving on a real single-screening-per-week cadence; the provenance and manifest-agreement checks still cover this source.

do215.note: v1 marked this 'partial' (events=8). A real JSON API (/events/YYYY/M/D.json) now backs this source (scripts/event_parsers/do215.py + scripts/collect_source.py) -- confirmed live 2026-07-29 against the real week of 2026-08-03: 467 events, not the 8-60 every prior estimate assumed. Almost all of the volume is legitimate but repetitive (e.g. a museum's daily guided tour re-listed as a distinct dated event on each of its 5 occurrences that week) with no structural field distinguishing it from a genuine one-off -- this is exactly the case event-selection-philosophy's 'Avoid: recurring weekly events' rule exists for, but that rule has never had to operate at this volume from a single source. Floor kept low and deliberately not raised to the true yield, since the real number this source contributes to a week's total_events_after_dedup is now an open question for Selection, not Collection, to absorb.

iffy-books.note: Google Calendar via MCP. Historical range 4-8; floor set with margin since the true minimum in a slow week is unconfirmed.

lightbox-film-center.note: A deterministic two-stage parser now backs this source (scripts/event_parsers/lightbox.py + scripts/collect_source.py: Wix data-hook index -> per-event JSON-LD detail pages) -- confirmed live 2026-07-29: 2 real events for the week of 2026-07-27 (a week v2 had previously collected as 0), and genuinely 0 for the week of 2026-08-03 (listings jump Aug 1 -> Sep 9). Kept at 0 rather than raised, since 0 is a real, frequent, correct result for this source, not evidence of failure -- the provenance and manifest-agreement checks still cover it.

luma.note: Historical range 5-10 across weeks of 2026-08-03 through -08-24 (never below 5, hence the prior floor). The scheduled 2026-08-30 run for the week of 2026-08-31 wrote 2 and tripped that floor -- verified directly against a live fetch of the same iCal feed: 2 real, well-formed events (a Beyonce-tribute pop-up and an online DIY book-cover workshop), not a parser or feed failure. Lowered to 2 to reflect this confirmed low rather than treat it as a recurring false positive, same reasoning as the r5-productions and the-rotunda precedents below.

meetup-ai-philly.note: Confirmed genuinely empty every observed run (well-formed iCal, 0 VEVENTs). Parser's own structural validation (raises only if BEGIN:VCALENDAR is absent) already covers this source; yield-floor adds nothing.

meetup-code-coffee.note: Active group but weekly count is genuinely variable (0-4 observed); relies on the parser's own structural validation, not a yield floor, to avoid false positives on a quiet week.

meetup-philadelphia-horror-meetup-group.note: Same reasoning as meetup-code-coffee. Renamed 2026-08-01 from meetup-horror to match what the Collection Routine actually writes -- SKILL.md documents the output filename as meetup-horror.json (line 59), but the real 2026-08-03 run wrote meetup-philadelphia-horror-meetup-group.json (the Meetup group's URL slug) instead. Content and source field are correct, only the filename deviates. Accepted as the de facto convention rather than fixed at the source, since the data itself was never wrong.

philadelphia-film-society.note: A resilient collector now backs this source (scripts/event_parsers/philadelphia_film_society.py + scripts/collect_source.py): 3 venues x 2 sample days (Wed+Sat), each fetch isolated so one hanging venue/day no longer fails the whole source -- confirmed live 2026-08-01: 18 events for the week of 2026-08-03, zero fetch failures, replacing a real prior week where the whole source reported status:failed. Still browser-only (Fandango showtimes are JS-rendered; Agile Ticketing, the real backend, is WAF-blocked same as filmadelphia.org). Floor set well below the confirmed 18 since only 2 of 7 days are sampled and yield will vary by what's actually programmed that week.

philly-ask-a-punk.note: Deterministic parser (Gancio API). One real incident (2026-07-21) where a WebFetch-routed fetch was silently truncated and returned 0 -- floor set to catch a repeat without false-positiving on a slower week. Historical non-incident range was 10-12 prior to 2026-08-10; the first real workflow_dispatch run of the GHA collection pipeline (2026-08-10) confirmed a genuine 5-event week -- verified directly: 5 well-formed events, real bands/venues/URLs, not an extraction failure. Lowered from 6 to 4 to reflect this real observed low without re-litigating it as a false positive every time DIY show volume dips.

phillygoth.note: Deterministic parser. Historical legitimate range 2-7 (excludes the 2026-07-27 fabricated 0); floor set at the low end.

r5-productions.note: Deterministic parser. Historical range was 7/week across all runs prior to 2026-08-03 -- floor of 5 was calibrated against that alone. The real 2026-08-03 run confirmed a genuine 2-event week (verified directly: 2 well-formed events, real venue/price/URL, not an extraction failure) and correctly tripped check_yield.py's floor; lowered to 2 at the time. The scheduled 2026-08-30 run for the week of 2026-08-31 wrote 1 and tripped that floor in turn -- verified directly against a live fetch of the events page: 1 real, well-formed event (Successor Tour, Spike Hellis @ Ruba Club, 2026-09-05), not an extraction failure. Lowered again to 1 for the same reason as before: a confirmed-legitimate quiet week is not a recurring false positive to chase.

the-rotunda.note: Deterministic parser. Historical range was 3-5/week across all runs prior to 2026-08-03 -- floor of 2 was calibrated against that alone. The real 2026-08-03 run confirmed a genuine 1-event week (verified directly: a real, well-formed event) and correctly tripped check_yield.py's floor. Lowered to 1 to reflect this real observed low rather than treat one confirmed-legitimate quiet week as a recurring false positive.
